prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the nearby girl, roughly 2–3 m in front of the camera wearer, from the more distant fence and terrain; a very bright, partly cropped foreground region at the bottom is within about 0–0.5 m of the camera. The girl remains well below the fence in the image and several metres in front of it, while shifting from the left side in frame 1 toward the centre-left in frames 2–4 and the right side in frame 5 as the camera turns. Her similar depth and apparent size suggest little approach or retreat, although frame 5 may place her slightly nearer. This relative distance ordering is clearer than in RGB, but glare-like bright regions near the top and bottom, blurred boundaries, and inconsistent fence brightness make exact metre estimates unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates one person about 2–3 m ahead, while marking a partly cropped cell phone or hand-held foreground object at the bottom of frames 1–2, within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach. It also marks a small sports ball near the lower-left of frame 3, roughly 1–2 m from the camera and about 1–2 m left of the person; most of the fence, ground, rocks, and other foreground items are not classified. The person moves across the image from left to centre-left to right without strong evidence of a large depth change, and no separate person is reliably visible behind her. The masks clarify object identity and occlusion boundaries, but the bottom-edge “person” region in frame 2 and fragmented phone masks appear unreliable, while the person masks omit fine limbs and cannot establish precise distances or gaze.
descriptions.pose: The pose map shows the same person’s body configuration in all five frames: she is upright about 2–3 m in front of the wearer, generally facing toward or obliquely toward the camera rather than fully away, although head direction and eye contact cannot be determined reliably. Her skeleton shifts from the left in frame 1 through centre-left in frames 2–4 to the right in frame 5, with modest changes in shoulder, arm, and leg orientation indicating turning or camera-relative viewpoint change rather than clear approach or retreat. Her arms remain close to her torso and do not reach the camera wearer or the detected ball; only the camera wearer’s cropped foreground hand or object is plausibly within the wearer’s arm’s reach. The skeleton makes limb placement and partial self-occlusion clearer than RGB, but several joints are missing or displaced, no magenta hand landmarks appear, and frame 5 is absent or too incomplete to support a detailed pose reading.
